title: The stages of the Exodus
summary: Moses' list of the 41 camps between Rameses and the plains of Moab. The route follows OpenBible.info's top-ranked identification for each camp, which puts Mount Sinai in the south of the peninsula (the traditional route). About a third of the camps have no agreed site. Where OpenBible only says a camp was near the one before, the camp is spaced along the line of travel and marked ≈. Legs are straight lines between camps unless the coastline forces a detour.

sources.note: The itinerary itself, camp by camp.
Links Moserah, Bene-jaakan, Gudgodah and Jotbathah, and puts Aaron's death at Moserah.

title: The borders of Canaan
summary: The boundary God gives Moses for the land, traced clockwise from the southern tip of the Salt Sea: west across the Negev to the Brook of Egypt, up the Mediterranean coast, east through Lebo-hamath to Hazar-enan, and back down past the Sea of Galilee and the Jordan. Named points use OpenBible.info's top-ranked identification. Where the text names a feature (the Brook, the coast, the Jordan, the Salt Sea), the line follows it. Where a point is unidentified, it is spaced between its neighbours and marked ≈. The identifications of the northern points are disputed.

sources.note: The boundary description itself.
Judah's southern border repeats the same line: Akrabbim, Zin, Kadesh-barnea, Hezron/Addar, Azmon, the Brook of Egypt.
Ezekiel's ideal borders repeat the northern and eastern line: Lebo-hamath, Zedad, Hazar-enan, the Jordan.

title: Saul from Jerusalem to Damascus and Tarsus
summary: Saul sets out from Jerusalem with letters to the synagogues of Damascus, is blinded on the road and led into the city, escapes over the wall, returns to Jerusalem and is sent off from Caesarea to Tarsus. Sites follow OpenBible.info's top-ranked identification. Acts does not say whether he went from Caesarea to Tarsus by sea, and the line is drawn straight. Paul's own account adds a stay in Arabia before he returned to Damascus (Gal 1:17), which Acts does not mention.

sources.note: The journey itself.
Paul's own account: 'I went into Arabia and later returned to Damascus. Only after three years did I go up to Jerusalem.'

title: From Antioch through Cyprus to Lycaonia
summary: Barnabas and Saul, sent out by the church at Antioch, sail from Seleucia to Cyprus, cross the island to Paphos, sail to Perga and go inland to Pisidian Antioch, Iconium and the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe, then go back the way they came and sail home from Attalia. Lightfoot (1890), who numbers the journeys of 15:40 and 18:23 second and third, makes this the first. Sites follow OpenBible.info's top-ranked identification. Legs are straight between the places named, except where a leg at sea is kept off the land.

title: From Antioch to Macedonia and Achaia
summary: Paul and Silas go back through Syria and Cilicia to the churches of Lycaonia, where Timothy joins them, are kept out of Asia and Bithynia, and cross from Troas to Macedonia: Philippi, Thessalonica and Berea, then Athens and a year and a half at Corinth. Paul sails home by Ephesus and Caesarea. Lightfoot (1890) calls it Paul's 'second missionary journey'. Sites follow OpenBible.info's top-ranked identification. Where Acts names a region and not a town the point is marked ≈, and the region of Phrygia and Galatia (16:6), which readers place differently, is drawn on neither reading. Paths between the places named are estimates.

Lightfoot (1890) calls it Paul's 'third missionary journey'. Sites follow OpenBible.info's top-ranked identification. Where Acts names a region and not a town the point is marked ≈, and the region of Galatia and Phrygia (18:23), which readers place differently, is drawn on neither reading. Paths between the places named are estimates.

title: The voyage to Rome

Sites follow OpenBible.info's top-ranked identification. Where the text gives the ship's course (the lee of Cyprus, the coast of Crete) the line follows it; across the storm it is drawn straight, since Acts gives no course.
